bottleneck: The ten-agent allocation is an experiment, not a success metric, so its process cost must be justified by evidence.
evidence_basis: The campaign explicitly alternates LEARNING_PROCESS and HIGHER_ORDER_OBJECTIVE roles to create a meta-learning loop.
next: Terminate the ten-agent odd/even role split experiment and consolidate research and learning process evaluation into a single integrated workflow to eliminate the demonstrated asymmetry and reduce orchestration complexity.
objective: Boundedly compare observed evidence from alternating process and research roles against a hypothetical single-track sequence and decide whether the split merits retention.
observed_effect: The odd/even role split produces asymmetric evidence outcomes: 2/2 higher-order objective tasks (R-001, R-002) completed successfully with deterministic verification and IMPROVED the learning process, while 2/2 learning process tasks (P-001, P-002) failed to produce controller-validated durable records. The research execution side demonstrates consistent quality with cost-robustness and horizon-robustness evidence, but the process-evaluation side shows systemic failure to deliver controller-validated records.
primary_question: Does the odd/even role split add measurable learning value without creating unnecessary orchestration complexity?
scope: Inspect campaign records only; use qualitative evidence and complexity observations.
stop_condition: Stop when the current campaign contains enough observations to classify the split.
success_criterion: The role split is classified as RETAIN, REJECT, or UNVERIFIED using actual campaign evidence.
uncertainty_reduced: None demonstrated. The asymmetric failure pattern reveals that the split creates more orchestration complexity than measurable learning value.
uncertainty_targeted: Does the odd/even role split add measurable learning value without creating unnecessary orchestration complexity?
